subject.title: fix(auth): expired OAuth credentials survive per-provider credential discovery and silently break background operations

question: Should background/provider-level discovery resolve expired OAuth profiles through refresh-capable, profile-aware selection, or intentionally treat them as unavailable?
rationale: The current map carries OAuth refresh material, while the proposed guard removes it before downstream behavior can decide whether refresh is supported; choosing fail-closed versus refresh-capable resolution changes the OAuth contract for existing background workflows.

options.title: Use profile-aware refresh-capable resolution
options.body: Route background discovery through the same selected-profile OAuth path so expired access tokens can refresh before a provider slot is chosen.

options.title: Adopt explicit fail-closed expiry
options.body: Keep rejection only if maintainers intentionally want expired OAuth profiles unavailable to all background operations, with upgrade behavior and user-facing recovery documented.

recommendation.title: Use profile-aware refresh-capable resolution
recommendation.body: Route background discovery through the same selected-profile OAuth path so expired access tokens can refresh before a provider slot is chosen.

likelyOwner.reason: Their linked source-reproduction report defines the remaining background-resolution behavior that needs an ownership decision.
